gpu: Two complete model/seed cohorts use eight additional GPUs. Each model uses four fixed contiguous eight-request slices of the unchanged 32 official requests. Every method uses identical prompt-to-device/core assignments. Each prompt keeps its original batch, first pass, warmup, three repetitions and 16 decode steps. Aggregate per-request latency, never sum GPU throughput. Retain earlier single-device samples as diagnostics.
preflight: Every new GPU runs source/native byte-equality checks on two actual batch-8 requests from its registered slice before timing.
cpu: Eight disjoint physical cores on the new host execute full CPU query measurements concurrently with GPU work. These are shared-host measurements. Serial reference queries wait until all GPU work on that host completes. Original-host GPU timing may continue on a different physical machine.
provenance: Record actual host, GPU UUID, CPU topology, request slice, child report hashes and complete canonical coverage. Original quality grids, training exposures, frozen choices and request budgets remain unchanged.
